entries.lesson_title: System Output from Input and Impulse Response
entries.core_move: Compute the LTI system output by evaluating the continuous-time convolution integral for a given input signal and impulse response.
Partition a direct convolution calculation into time regions by tracking how the overlap between $x(\tau)$ and $h(t - \tau)$ changes as t moves.
Compute the convolution of finite-duration input and impulse-response signals by finding overlap intervals, setting integration bounds, and assembling the piecewise LTI output.
Evaluate direct convolution involving sloped signal segments by expressing the overlapping pieces in $\tau$, setting time-dependent bounds, and integrating the resulting products.
Convert each time-region overlap in a direct convolution into geometric area calculations to obtain the piecewise LTI system output.

entries.lesson_title: Checking Continuity of a Convolution Result
entries.core_move: Verify a piecewise convolution result by comparing left- and right-hand boundary values at adjacent time regions to catch algebra or region errors.

entries.lesson_title: Interpreting Convolution as LTI System Output
entries.core_move: Interpret a piecewise convolution result as the time-domain output behavior of an LTI system determined jointly by the input signal and impulse response.
